title: As Jackery Inventory Sells Out, Are Portable Batteries Set To Take Off?
raw_summary: I recently wrote reviews of the new Jackery HomePower 1000 Plus v2 and Explorer 100D . A few days later, a connection with Jackery messaged me that their Black Friday/Cyber Monday products had largely sold out. Just three days after launching on November 1. This includes 1000, 2000, 3600 and 5000 portable power and solar generator models. Additional models have sold out since then or will likely sell out soon. The recently launched Explorer 100D is still available in limited quantities at Walmart and Costco. While Jackery will still take orders for Black Friday/Cyber Monday sales, most models currently listed for purchase will be on a preorder basis. Customers should check estimated delivery dates. Some restocking is expected in late November, although broader inventory availability may not recover until early next year.

This includes 1000, 2000, 3600 and 5000 portable power and solar generator models. Additional models have sold out since then or will likely sell out soon. The recently launched Explorer 100D is still available in limited quantities at Walmart and Costco.

While Jackery will still take orders for Black Friday/Cyber Monday sales, most models currently listed for purchase will be on a preorder basis. Customers should check estimated delivery dates. Some restocking is expected in late November, although broader inventory availability may not recover until early next year.

While much of America was recovering from Halloween and election victory parties, portable batteries were selling out. This wasn’t the result of limited supply, but rather a massive, unanticipated increase in demand.

Between October 19 th and 26 th , Jackery retail sales increased 755% at Costco, 106% at Walmart, 297% at The Home Depot and 442% at Lowes. For added perspective, at Costco alone, sales increased from 2379 to 20,343 over that one week.

Jackery is looking into what’s behind the massive increase in demand. Clearly, there have been climate-related disasters over the past year, including hurricanes and wildfires. Jackery’s collaboration with the Red Cross helps illustrate the benefits of portable power in emergency response. However, that only partially explains the growth. A related potential explanation is the growing push for household preparedness. There are reports of at least 17 countries encouraging people to keep three to seven days of food, water and other essentials. Winter storm season, grid strain and rising energy costs could be stoking fears of potential power outages. The US FORTRESS America initiative has also added an emphasis on resilience. Together, these signals may be pushing “preparedness” beyond food and water to include power.

Preparedness is gaining emphasis with power becoming an increasingly important part of being prepared. The fear of “what if” can be a powerful motivator. Having backup power can keep the air handlers working for people’s furnaces. People on well water can keep the pumps running. Backup power can keep refrigerators full of food from spoiling.

Overall, Jackery is the global leader in solar generator sales volume and was named the “World’s No.1 Solar Generator Brand” by Frost & Sullivan. With over 15 years of experience and extensive safety protocols, the brand is well established. For the purchase of a product that manages risks, having a trusted brand is clearly valuable.

Although there has not been a detailed study of the consumer motivations, preparedness is likely a major motivator. However, versatile portable power stations have additional benefits. I keep finding new ways to use the HomePower 1000 Plus V2. And new possible benefits keep opening up.

raw_title: America’s New Shipbuilding Orders Are Expensive Bets on Fossil Freight
title: America's New Shipbuilding Orders Are Expensive Bets on Fossil Freight
raw_summary: South Korea’s Hanwha Group owns the Philadelphia shipyard that has become a centerpiece of Washington’s attempt to rebuild American commercial shipbuilding. Its Hanwha Ocean and Hanwha Systems subsidiaries acquired the US yard in December 2024 . The investment creates and sustains American production capacity and jobs while transferring shipbuilding expertise, technology and training from South Korea to US workers. The facility is in America, but its corporate ownership remains South Korean. The company’s published orderbook , however, tells a more complicated story: two liquefied natural gas carriers, four firm orders for oil and chemical tankers, and options for another six tankers. Three LNG-fueled container ships ordered by Matson in 2022 predate the current administration. The newer LNG and tanker orders come from Hanwha’s own shipping affiliates. They can help restart production, but buying ships from another company in the same group does not demonstrate that independent shipowners will pay US construction prices. The price gap is difficult to dismiss. Kinder Morgan’s January 2026 investor presentation estimates that a new medium-range Jones Act tanker would cost more than $240 million and require a long-term charter above $115,000 per day to justify construction. The existing charter market was around $90,000 per day. Kinder Morgan operates 16 tankers, with its fleet fully utilized, yet the gap between current charter revenue and the cost of a replacement vessel remains substantial. High utilization establishes a need for shipping services; it does not establish a financeable order for a new American-built tanker at today’s prices.

They can help restart production, but buying ships from another company in the same group does not demonstrate that independent shipowners will pay US construction prices.

The price gap is difficult to dismiss. Kinder Morgan’s January 2026 investor presentation estimates that a new medium-range Jones Act tanker would cost more than $240 million and require a long-term charter above $115,000 per day to justify construction. The existing charter market was around $90,000 per day. Kinder Morgan operates 16 tankers, with its fleet fully utilized, yet the gap between current charter revenue and the cost of a replacement vessel remains substantial. High utilization establishes a need for shipping services; it does not establish a financeable order for a new American-built tanker at today’s prices.

Coastal petroleum shipping also competes with other domestic infrastructure. A 2025 report to the Commodity Futures Trading Commission estimated moving gasoline from Houston to New York Harbor at under 8 cents per gallon by pipeline, about 20 cents by ship, and roughly 35 cents by rail. These illustrative route costs do not cover every destination, and tankers remain essential where pipelines are unavailable. They do show why expensive new tankers cannot count on charter customers accepting whatever price domestic construction requires. Longer term, the International Energy Agency estimates that electric vehicles displaced 1.7 million barrels of oil per day worldwide in 2025 and could displace about 5 million by 2030 under its policy scenarios. That does not mean US tanker demand vanishes, but fleet investment must account for changes in the cargo market over several decades.

LNG export carriers have a more plausible near-term growth market, although their prospects are different from the prospects of LNG-fueled container ships. US gas exports may expand, and LNG tankers will be needed to carry them. The commercial test for a US-built LNG carrier is whether it can win an arm’s-length contract against established Korean, Japanese and Chinese shipyards. Hanwha’s plan to train Philadelphia workers through its Korean shipyards can strengthen US industrial capability, and affiliated orders can provide an initial production run. The central uncertainty is whether independent buyers will still choose these ships once the group’s internal demand and any cargo preference are removed.

A broader domestic vessel market already exists. US-flag Great Lakes freighters carried 71.3 million tons in 2025 , much of it iron ore, limestone, cement, coal and other bulk materials. Those cargo flows will change as steelmaking and energy systems evolve, while ferry services, harbour vessels, inland cargo craft and multipurpose ships will still require renewal. Battery-electric and hybrid-electric propulsion offer practical options on routes with manageable energy requirements and reliable charging access. Large, long-distance bulk ships need a more selective technology assessment, rather than an assumption that every vessel can run on batteries.

Recent projects demonstrate what a committed customer can contribute to ship economics. CMA CGM, Nike and Gemadept launched an electric inland barge in Vietnam for a 180-kilometre round trip. Nike agreed to fill 90% of its capacity for eight years , helping justify a vessel reportedly costing about twice as much as its diesel equivalent. A dedicated charging installation and renewable electricity form part of the service. That is a commercially structured freight proposition, with its higher capital cost supported by contracted utilization and expected operating savings.

Electric propulsion does not cure the American shipbuilding cost problem by itself. Washington State’s three new hybrid-electric ferries carry a $714.5 million shipbuilding contract , and the state’s estimate including additional equipment and other program expenses is approximately $1.15 billion. Construction has started; the ferries are not yet in service. The path to a productive shipbuilding industry still runs through standardized designs, modular fabrication, trained workers, repeat orders, reliable delivery and falling labor-hours per vessel. It would be a mistake to treat electrification as a substitute for manufacturing reform.

Hanwha’s South Korean capital and know-how could contribute to that reform by developing US suppliers and production skills that serve several vessel classes. That is a meaningful way to rebuild domestic capability even though the parent company remains foreign-owned. Its progress should ultimately be measured by independent repeat customers, improving construction costs and commercially competitive vessels, rather than affiliated orders or investment announcements. A US maritime strategy anchored to the fossil-fuel cargoes of today risks missing a growing opportunity to build modern domestic vessels for the freight, port and ferry services of tomorrow.

raw_summary: Kia is expanding its electric van lineup with the PV7, a larger PV5 sibling that can carry nine people or a whole lot of cargo. The PV5, Kia’s first fully electric van from its Platform Beyond Vehicle (PBV) business, is proving to be a bigger hit than expected.
summary: Kia is expanding its electric van lineup with the PV7, a larger PV5 sibling that can carry nine people or a whole lot of cargo. The PV5, Kia’s first fully electric van from its Platform Beyond Vehicle (PBV) business, is proving to be a bigger hit than expected.
article_paragraphs: Kia is expanding its electric van lineup with the PV7, a larger PV5 sibling that can carry nine people or a whole lot of cargo.
The PV5, Kia’s first fully electric van from its Platform Beyond Vehicle (PBV) business, is proving to be a bigger hit than expected.

A year after it went on sale, the PV5 quickly became Europe’s most popular small electric van. In the first half of 2026, it was the top seller in its segment, accounting for 37% of electric C-segment van sales across Europe.
Next year, Kia will launch the PV7, the second electric van from its PBV business. Kia revealed the PV7 at IAA Transportation in Hanover, Germany, in September.
It’s based on the same E-GMP.S platform as the PV5, but the PV7 features a considerably longer wheelbase and stretched body, opening up more space inside.

The PV7 is over 17.5 ft long, measuring 5,350 mm long, 1,995 mm wide, and 1,990 mm high, with a 3,500 mm wheelbase. In comparison, the PV5 is just 4,695 mm long, 1,895 mm wide, and 1,915 mm tall, with a 2,995 mm wheelbase.
That’s even bigger than the Volkswagen ID. Buzz Long-Wheelbase (LWB), which measures 4,962 mm in length with a 3,239 mm wheelbase.
Like the PV5, the PV7 will initially be available in Passenger and Cargo body styles, but Kia plans to launch 23 different variants, or “top hats,” over the next few years.

raw_summary: Somehow, despite buying a used 2006 Ducati Monster with more than 20,000 miles on the odometer and having done no pre-purchase inspection, my bike ended up being pretty darn reliable. I had a feeling it would be based on the way the previous owner had cared for and modified it, and they'd clearly loved riding it, but other than replacing the front fork seals, I didn't have to do any work to it the entire time I lived in the Los Angeles metro area. Ducati may be the Ferrari of motorcycles, but it sure didn't feel like it based on running costs. If you know motorcycles, you know that's because Ducati Monsters are pretty darn reliable. Non-motorcycle people tend to see the bright paint, wild styling, and Italian heritage and assume Monsters are in the shop just as often as an '80s Lamborghini. That got me thinking — surely, I can't be the only one who's owned vehicles that ended up being more reliable and cheaper to own than other people tend to assume.

If you know motorcycles, you know that's because Ducati Monsters are pretty darn reliable. Non-motorcycle people tend to see the bright paint, wild styling, and Italian heritage and assume Monsters are in the shop just as often as an '80s Lamborghini. That got me thinking — surely, I can't be the only one who's owned vehicles that ended up being more reliable and cheaper to own than other people tend to assume.

So I asked for your examples , and boy, let me tell you. I did not need the encouragement some of your stories are giving me. Despite the horror stories, part of me wants to replace the Fiat with a BMW i8 , and I'm going to have to get incredibly lucky if I'm going to pull that off without ruining my finances. But that doesn't mean I didn't enjoy the encouragement. Let's take a look at some of the most popular answers.

My 2014 Panamera 4 has been 100% rock-solid. I have done only routine maintenance except. Maintance isn't always cheap HOWEVER the car is one of the most reliable cars I have ever owned and now that I do my own oil changes (and might try brakes when they are due), the cost will drop even more.

Second has been the two Abarths I have owned (still have my 2014 that I autocross). The internet makes it seem like these cars will break-down as much as the old Fiat 124's but these cars have never let me down. In fact, working on my Abarth is extremely easy. There is a huge fanbase so finding videos or advice on modifying or DIY maintenance on these cars is easy. I push the Abarth all the time and it takes it.
I've been daily driving an 87 Alfa Romeo Milano for 7 years now. It's been off the road maybe 2 weeks total during that time, sometimes for optional upgrades.

I've heard endless thoughts, jokes, etc about the infamous "Alfa reliability", all from people who have never owned an Alfa. I get my laughs from my neighbor, who has often given his thoughts. He has a Toyota pickup of the same era that has driven 7000 less miles than the Alfa over our decade as neighbors due to constant issues.
2011 WRX right from the factory. Deep in the middle of the whole ring land fiasco. Here we are in 2026 and it's still standing, 170k+ later.

title: Lincoln Is Bringing Back the Plug-In Hybrid Aviator in China
raw_summary: Lincoln used to sell the Aviator SUV with an optional plug-in hybrid powertrain, but it was dropped from the lineup after 2023 . Now, there’s a new Aviator PHEV in town, only this time, the towns it will be driving in will exclusively be across the Pacific Ocean. This is the Lincoln Aviator EX8, designed specifically for China and revealed via a regulatory filing with China’s Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT). Developed as part of Ford’s joint venture with Chinese automaker Changan, the new Aviator EX8 looks completely different from the Aviator SUV sold on our shores. It’s handsome and confident, with a blockier shape and an upright front end, and the large rectangular grille is adorned with a series of cascading chrome trim pieces. A large U-shaped trim piece spans the base of the front fascia, giving the SUV a planted look. It’s about the same size as the Aviator sold here, coming in a tad shorter, about an inch narrower, and roughly an inch taller. The rear is simple, with just a full-width rectangular taillight.

A large U-shaped trim piece spans the base of the front fascia, giving the SUV a planted look. It’s about the same size as the Aviator sold here, coming in a tad shorter, about an inch narrower, and roughly an inch taller. The rear is simple, with just a full-width rectangular taillight.

The EX8 is motivated by a plug-in hybrid powertrain. It uses a 1.5-liter turbocharged four-cylinder engine from Changan that produces 148 horsepower, but the MIIT documents didn’t reveal any details on the number of electric motors, their positioning, or their output. In 2025, Changan launched a range-extender PHEV SUV called the Nevo Q07, which comes in single- and dual-motor configurations with up to 389 hp and a total range of 870 miles.

The Aviator EX8 is expected to get its proper reveal at the Guangzhou auto show later this month before going on sale in China next year. We can pretty definitively say that the Aviator EX8 will never be sold in the U.S., but we hope to see a hybrid Aviator return to our shores at some point in the future.

I want to know what car leaves zero doubt that someone has to sit separately from his ex-wife at school functions for fear that there could be an incident.

I'm not going to be too much of a stickler about the car you pick, either. It can be new or used, because classic cars definitely have an air of divorce about them, too, and so do cheap used cars — especially if divorce court didn't go your way.

For my pick for this question, I'm going with something new to keep it interesting. The answer to which car screams "I'm divorced!" is the Dodge Charger Sixpack R/T — the Hurricane inline-six-powered Dodge muscle car. Specifically, it has to be the two-door coupe, because you're only seeing the kids on weekends, anyway. Why do you need easy access to the rear seats? Exactly.

The car has everything the modern divorced man needs: throwback looks to a time when their hair wasn't thinning, a big enough trunk to hold the toys they're going to bribe their kids with, and even a reasonable starting price at $51,990, including destination. Add in the 420 horsepower it produces and the fact it'll do zero to 60 mph in 4.6 seconds (fast enough to outrun your demons and the alimony payments), and you've got a winner on your hands. Of course, you could always go for the more expensive Charger Sixpack Scat Pack, but court was never going to let you off the hook that easily, so you've got to save where you can.

Anyway, that's enough out of me. How about you all head on down below and let your fellow Jalops know what cars scream "I'm divorced"? As always, I'll love you more if you tell me why you made your pick.

title: Too Much Motion in the Ocean: We Test the 2027 Mercedes-Benz GLS450
raw_summary: You can have the world’s best cartographers in your employ, and your ship can still end up drifting off course. The 2027 Mercedes-Benz GLS450 is one such boat. Mercedes has buildings full of nitpicky engineers whose sole collective life goal is to build the most comfortable three-row SUV on terra firma. And while the result of the GLS’s latest refresh largely hits the mark, we believe this ute’s ride quality missed its intended landing zone. Let’s focus on the high points first. We’re big fans of the base GLS450’s 3.0-liter turbocharged inline-six. Thanks to a stronger electric supercharger and a few other updates, this powertrain now spits out 375 horsepower and 413 pound-feet of torque fed through a nine-speed automatic transmission to all four wheels. With it, the GLS450 managed a solid 5.1-second sprint to 60, eventually clearing the quarter-mile mark in an equally respectable 13.6 seconds at 101 mph. Not bad for a gas-powered machine that tipped our scales at 5623 pounds.
summary: You can have the world’s best cartographers in your employ, and your ship can still end up drifting off course. The 2027 Mercedes-Benz GLS450 is one such boat. Mercedes has buildings full of nitpicky engineers whose sole collective life goal is to build the most comfortable three-row SUV on terra firma.
article_paragraphs: You can have the world’s best cartographers in your employ, and your ship can still end up drifting off course. The 2027 Mercedes-Benz GLS450 is one such boat. Mercedes has buildings full of nitpicky engineers whose sole collective life goal is to build the most comfortable three-row SUV on terra firma. And while the result of the GLS’s latest refresh largely hits the mark, we believe this ute’s ride quality missed its intended landing zone.

Let’s focus on the high points first. We’re big fans of the base GLS450’s 3.0-liter turbocharged inline-six. Thanks to a stronger electric supercharger and a few other updates, this powertrain now spits out 375 horsepower and 413 pound-feet of torque fed through a nine-speed automatic transmission to all four wheels. With it, the GLS450 managed a solid 5.1-second sprint to 60, eventually clearing the quarter-mile mark in an equally respectable 13.6 seconds at 101 mph. Not bad for a gas-powered machine that tipped our scales at 5623 pounds.

Out in the real world, the powertrain only ever feels smooth. Whether we’re stomping on the right pedal or just breathing on it, the result is the same: a muted little growl and plenty of grunt. The transmission stays out of the spotlight; in fact, everything hiding under the body does its best to stay out of earshot. Our microphones picked up very little cabin noise, recording just 65 decibels (20 sones) at a 70-mph cruise. Insofar as high-end family transportation goes, the GLS450 nails that part of its assignment.

The GLS450’s cabin also succeeds in its goals—mostly. The materials are standard Mercedes-Benz fare, with plenty of nice-feeling leather and vinyl up top, while most of the harder materials remain low in the cabin, away from traditional touch points. Our test car had the no-charge six-seater option; the captain’s chairs in the second row are cushy and make third-row ingress and egress a breeze. The car’s so dang large that even adults can be reasonably comfortable all the way in back, with decent headroom and legroom that’s fine for short jaunts around town.

However, our editors didn’t fully embrace the cabin’s centerpiece: the Superscreen. This panoply of digital real estate spans the entire width of the dashboard, with a single piece of glass encasing the digital gauge cluster, the primary infotainment touchscreen, and the optional (and wholly superfluous) passenger screen. It’s basically eliminated the need to design a dashboard, which does a disservice to those who appreciate an aesthetic other than Blade Runner Dystopia. In fact, this pixel addiction is a growing problem across the entire Mercedes lineup. But hey, at least the steering wheel picked up a physical rocker and a thumbwheel.

When it comes to the external half of the GLS-class’s refresh, the whole look gels, but like the revised S-class sedan before it, we’re wondering if Mercedes is going too hard in the paint on the self-branding. In addition to the gigantic three-pointed star on the grille, the grille itself now contains dozens of little three-pointed stars. Each headlight now has two three-pointed stars acting as running lights. In total, the rear lights contain six three-pointed stars. It’s a great design if you’re constantly forgetting what car you bought. Who are they trying to sell this thing to, the protagonist from Memento ?

The GLS450’s more prominent bugbear is its ride quality. Ordinarily, a plush ride means road inconsistencies disappear, replaced with a body that floats serenely over juts and ruts without transmitting undue movement to the cabin and its occupants. In the GLS450, though, it appears the suspension engineers were tasked with reinventing body-on-frame jiggle from first principles. On any road that isn’t obsidian smooth, the GLS suffers from an awful lot of lateral wobbling after tackling a bump, and the body barely settles down by the time the next one arrives. It’s as if the engineers benchmarked an unladen F-350. Our test car was riding on the stock air suspension, and while it’s possible that upgrading to the electrohydraulic E-Active Body Control system would eliminate these unwanted movements, we’re let down that this setup ever left the plant in Alabama.

Despite a terminal case of the Wibbly-Wobblies, GLS450 proved surprisingly sticky around our 300-foot skidpad. We managed 0.92 g of lateral grip from the Pirelli P Zero PZ5 summer tires (285/40R-23 front, 325/35R-23 rear). The GLS also stopped from 70 mph in a tidy 154 feet. We’d appreciate these stats more if they didn’t come attached to a four-wheeled waterbed.

title: Tesla hikes Cybertruck prices up to 10% after announcing it will kill production
raw_summary: Tesla has raised Cybertruck prices in the US by up to 10% and stopped taking orders for the base Dual Motor AWD trim. The cheapest Cybertruck you can actually order now costs $92,490. The move comes right after Tesla confirmed it will end Cybertruck production at Gigafactory Texas around mid-2027.
summary: Tesla has raised Cybertruck prices in the US by up to 10% and stopped taking orders for the base Dual Motor AWD trim. The cheapest Cybertruck you can actually order now costs $92,490. The move comes right after Tesla confirmed it will end Cybertruck production at Gigafactory Texas around mid-2027.
article_paragraphs: Tesla has raised Cybertruck prices in the US by up to 10% and stopped taking orders for the base Dual Motor AWD trim. The cheapest Cybertruck you can actually order now costs $92,490.
The move comes right after Tesla confirmed it will end Cybertruck production at Gigafactory Texas around mid-2027.
Here’s what Tesla’s online configurator shows today, compared to the prices set in August:
The Dual Motor trim still shows a new, higher price on Tesla’s website, but the option is greyed out. So Tesla raised the price of a version it isn’t selling anymore.

This is the second price hike in less than three months. Tesla raised prices by $5,000 on two trims in August , when the Dual Motor went from $69,990 to $74,990 and the Premium AWD from $79,990 to $84,990.

Add it up and the Premium AWD is now $12,500 (15.6%) more expensive than it was in early August. And the entry price for any Cybertruck you can order went from $69,990 to $92,490. That’s a 32% jump in about 10 weeks.
For reference, Tesla unveiled the Cybertruck in 2019 with a promised starting price of $39,900.

The price hikes make little sense from a demand standpoint. Tesla doesn’t break out Cybertruck deliveries, but its “Other Models” category, which also includes the Model S, Model X, and Semi, fell 48% year-over-year to 8,295 units in Q3. We estimate Cybertrucks made up 7,000 to 8,000 of those, about 12% of the line’s 250,000-unit annual capacity.

According to Musk’s post, Tesla will wind down “production of the Cybertruck at Gigafactory Texas around the middle of next year,” indicating that the 2027 model year will be its last. Admittedly, it’s possible that the company moves the Cybertruck’s production elsewhere. This seems unlikely, though, given the middling sales figures of the model, which continue to fall far short of the annual 250,000-unit production figure predicted early on by Musk.

Tesla sold 38,965 Cybertrucks in 2024, though that number fell to just 20,237 in 2025. Cybertruck sales continue to trend downward for Tesla, which sold just 11,586 units through the first three quarters of 2026.

Of course, the battery-powered pickup ’s high price didn’t help its cause. Currently, Tesla is limiting Cybertruck orders to the roughly $90,000 Premium All-Wheel Drive and the six-figure Cyberbeast trims. The more than $80,000 Dual-Motor All-Wheel Drive variant remains listed on the Tesla site, indicating the automaker may open orders for that trim again before production ends.

Despite their shared last name, Greg Fink is not related to Ed "Big Daddy" Roth's infamous Rat Fink. Both Finks, however, are known for their love of cars, car culture, and—strangely—monogrammed one-piece bathing suits. Greg's career in the media industry goes back more than a decade. His previous experience includes stints as an editor at publications such as U.S. News & World Report , The Huffington Post, Motor1.com , and MotorTrend .

raw_title: GM Could Make Variable-Compression Engines Easier to Service
title: GM Could Make Variable-Compression Engines Easier to Service
raw_summary: GM engineers spend a lot of time thinking about engines, and the company’s patent-to-production pipeline is hard evidence. Cylinder deactivation and sliding camshafts? GM has brought its own versions of both to production. Making truck V-8s bigger and more powerful without completely sacrificing efficiency? Coming right up . Their next target may be applying existing fuel-saving tech to a wider array of engines. A few engineers in particular have been tinkering with ways to adopt a variable-compression ratio, and specifically how the necessary hardware can be packaged with a longitudinal engine. Related patents go back about a decade. (Nissan already sells a variable-compression engine of its own, the somewhat disappointing VC-Turbo , but that one is designed for transverse front- and all-wheel-drive applications.)
summary: GM engineers spend a lot of time thinking about engines, and the company’s patent-to-production pipeline is hard evidence. Cylinder deactivation and sliding camshafts? GM has brought its own versions of both to production. Making truck V-8s bigger and more powerful without completely sacrificing efficiency? Their next target may be applying existing fuel-saving tech to a wider array of engines.
article_paragraphs: GM engineers spend a lot of time thinking about engines, and the company’s patent-to-production pipeline is hard evidence. Cylinder deactivation and sliding camshafts? GM has brought its own versions of both to production. Making truck V-8s bigger and more powerful without completely sacrificing efficiency? Coming right up . Their next target may be applying existing fuel-saving tech to a wider array of engines.

A few engineers in particular have been tinkering with ways to adopt a variable-compression ratio, and specifically how the necessary hardware can be packaged with a longitudinal engine. Related patents go back about a decade. (Nissan already sells a variable-compression engine of its own, the somewhat disappointing VC-Turbo , but that one is designed for transverse front- and all-wheel-drive applications.)

In a previous patent filing, GM outlined how it would locate the control shaft, necessary for varying compression in its design, up above the crankshaft. The compression variability—approximately 7:1 to 11:1—comes by way of a special connecting-rod linkage. The connecting rod attaches to one end of a center link that’s mounted on the crankshaft, and the other end of the center link connects through a control rod to the control shaft. The design also includes a phaser that adjusts the control shaft’s rotational timing relative to the crankshaft, thus controlling the piston’s movement and varying the compression.

And one bonus compared with Nissan's system, which uses valve timing to achieve the Atkinson-cycle effect, GM’s arrangement would allow for the expansion stroke to be longer than the compression stroke—up to 40 percent longer—which has potential efficiency benefits. Note that Honda has commercialized a similar extended-expansion engine concept, which it calls EXlink, that’s used in household cogeneration units that supply both electricity and hot water.

Now comes an innovation that could push a variable-compression longitudinal engine closer to reality. A recently published U.S. patent application shows how GM could make this happen. In a nutshell, it would replace the center link with a two-piece assembly assembled around the crankshaft. One part would connect to the piston rod, and the other to the control rod.

The description also says the bolts used to make up the connection would be accessible from below the engine, likely with the oil pan removed. GM also explains that placing the control shaft above the crankshaft makes room for the engine’s mounts or the vehicle’s steering or four-wheel-drive equipment that normally sit below a longitudinally oriented engine.

GM says this design would allow conventional lubrication of the connecting rods. Together with the two-piece center link, that could mean the GM design is both easier to service and less prone to bearing-related problems.

The patent drawings show a gas inline-six, a gasoline engine layout GM doesn’t currently use, but that’s not evidence that such a configuration is in the offing. The same concept could be applied to something like the L3B 2.7-liter four-cylinder —the one with sliding cam sleeves—that’s used in Chevy and GMC half-ton trucks and could find its way into a new Camaro or Buick sedan.

article_paragraphs: …JK! US President Donald Trump will never cry surrender in the war against offshore wind turbines. The President was burned once before, when a wind farm arose in Aberdeen Bay in Scotland, within view of a Trump-branded golf course back in the early 2000’s. Never again! The President has taken extreme measures to prevent such blight from tainting the shores of the United States. Nevertheless, scores of the pesky oversized pinwheels have already eluded the Trump chopper, and many more are on the way.

The latest news concerns CVOW, the 2.6-gigwatt Coastal Virginia Offshore Wind project under the wing of the leading utility Dominion. As the name of the project indicates, CVOW sits in the Atlantic Ocean about 24 nautical miles (28 land miles) off the coast of Virginia Beach, Virginia.
CVOW began taking shape during Trump’s first turn around the Oval Office, and construction was well under way when his second term began on January 20, 2025.

Immediately upon taking office, Trump abruptly suspended the offshore wind lease program administered by the Department of the Interior. He also ordered spurious re-reviews of offshore projects that were already in the permitting pipeline, and he had the Department of Justice administer a legally questionable buy-back program to prevent activity from stirring among other lease holders. In addition, he had the Interior Department issue multiple emergency orders aimed at stopping five offshore projects off the coasts of Rhode Island, Connecticut, New Jersey, New York, Maryland, and Massachusetts, where construction work was already well under way.

So far, though, only one part of the effort has stuck. Last year a federal judge affirmed that any President, Trump or not, has the authority to stop issuing new offshore leases. However, the same judge decided there is no blanket authority to suspend offshore leases that are already in the permitting process. The buy-back program is also in litigation, with critics raising questions about the funds used to pay off lease holders among other issues.
Additionally, the Interior Department failed to convince multiple federal judges that the emergency orders had any merit. Work has continued on all five Atlantic coast projects, including CVOW .

CVOW began delivering its first kilowatts to shore in March, and Dominion recapped its progress on the wind farm in its Q3 report on October 30. As handily summarized by the news organization Maritime Executive , the project currently clocks in at 85% complete. All of the main turbine components — nacelles, towers, and blades — for the wind farm’s 176 offshore wind turbines have been fabricated. Forty-four have been fully installed so far. With a 45th coming any day now, the wind farm currently hosts 640 megawatts out of the 2,600 megawatt total.

Since Trump declared an “Energy Emergency” in January of 2025, it’s fair to ask why he has spent so much time, energy and taxpayer dollars to crush an entire domestic energy industry. After all, if one was not reading too closely between the lines of the declaration, the new energy policy is little more than a rehash of former President Barack Obama’s “All Of The Above” energy policy. As further embellished by Energy Secretary Chris Wright, the new version specifically taps multiple zero and low-emission energy resources for support including nuclear energy, biomass, hydropower, and geothermal energy, just like Obama did, along the emerging field of marine energy, which was barely a speck on the horizon while Obama was in office.

title: Lucid teases its cheaper sub-$50,000 Cosmos EV in new video and images
raw_summary: Lucid has released a new teaser video of what looks like the Cosmos, its upcoming sub-$50,000 midsize electric SUV and the car that’s supposed to turn Lucid into a volume automaker. The clip gives us the clearest look yet at the Cosmos’ lighting, front and rear, after months of camouflaged prototype sightings. But the car itself is still about a year away.
summary: Lucid has released a new teaser video of what looks like the Cosmos, its upcoming sub-$50,000 midsize electric SUV and the car that’s supposed to turn Lucid into a volume automaker. The clip gives us the clearest look yet at the Cosmos’ lighting, front and rear, after months of camouflaged prototype sightings.
article_paragraphs: Lucid has released a new teaser video of what looks like the Cosmos, its upcoming sub-$50,000 midsize electric SUV and the car that’s supposed to turn Lucid into a volume automaker.
The clip gives us the clearest look yet at the Cosmos’ lighting, front and rear, after months of camouflaged prototype sightings. But the car itself is still about a year away.

Lucid posted the 1 minute 34 second video on X yesterday. The caption talks about “elevating the experience of movement” and says Lucid can’t wait “to share this feeling with even more people.” It doesn’t name the vehicle, but “even more people” is about as subtle a hint at a cheaper model as you can get.

Two frames from the film show the vehicle at dusk. At the rear, “LUCID” is spelled out in red illuminated letters across the tailgate, flanked by thin red light strips, with a spoiler cutting across the base of the rear glass. Up front, a sculpted LED headlight with a row of vertical segments sweeps across a red body panel.

That rear end matches the Cosmos design Lucid registered with the EU Intellectual Property Office in May, which showed the same spelled-out “LUCID” tailgate and rear-glass spoiler. It also lines up with the thin red light strips on the camouflaged Cosmos prototype spotted on Highway 101 in California last month.
Lucid unveiled its plans for Cosmos and Earth at its first Investor Day in March . Both ride on the new midsize platform and start under $50,000, roughly half the price of the Gravity.

On paper, the Cosmos is impressive. Lucid claims about 300 miles of range from a 69 kWh pack, thanks to efficiency of up to 4.5 mi/kWh, which it says is 10% better than its closest competitor. It also claims 200 miles of range in 14 minutes of charging, and its new Atlas drive unit has 30% fewer parts and costs 37% less than the Zeus unit in the Gravity.
The problem is timing. Production was supposed to start in late 2026. In August, CEO Silvio Napoli pushed the Cosmos to 2027 , “most likely the second half.”

raw_title: This 1,000 HP Dodge Power Wagon Is Actually A TRX Underneath
title: This 1,000 HP Dodge Power Wagon Is Actually A TRX Underneath
raw_summary: The Dodge Power Wagon dates back to the mid-1940s, and while this example may look like an original that's been modernized, it's actually something else entirely. Built by Desert Power Wagons in North Carolina, it started life as a 2021 Ram 1500 TRX. If you want a pickup that looks like a classic but performs like a modern truck, something like this might be perfect. Known as Project Colossus, the Ram's chassis has been modified to support a third axle and two extra wheels. Those new rear wheels aren't just along for the ride and disconnected from the powertrain as we've seen on other 6x6 projects. Instead, this wild truck has a full-time BorgWarner transfer case delivering 6WD Auto, 6WD High, and 6WH Low operating ranges, plus a Dana 60 rear axle and an electronically locking differential. It also has Bilstein Black Hawk e2 active shock absorbers and Black Rhino wheels with 38-inch Toyo Open Country R/T tires.

article_paragraphs: The Dodge Power Wagon dates back to the mid-1940s, and while this example may look like an original that's been modernized, it's actually something else entirely. Built by Desert Power Wagons in North Carolina, it started life as a 2021 Ram 1500 TRX. If you want a pickup that looks like a classic but performs like a modern truck, something like this might be perfect.

Known as Project Colossus, the Ram's chassis has been modified to support a third axle and two extra wheels. Those new rear wheels aren't just along for the ride and disconnected from the powertrain as we've seen on other 6x6 projects. Instead, this wild truck has a full-time BorgWarner transfer case delivering 6WD Auto, 6WD High, and 6WH Low operating ranges, plus a Dana 60 rear axle and an electronically locking differential. It also has Bilstein Black Hawk e2 active shock absorbers and Black Rhino wheels with 38-inch Toyo Open Country R/T tires.

The distinctive bodywork is the most significant change made. It features a four-door crew cab from Tisdale Coachworkers that almost perfectly mimics a classic Power Wagon. The front end is also just like an original and has similar headlights positioned on the front fenders and a brutish steel front bumper, now incorporating a heavy-duty winch. Adding to the truck's wild design is a stealthy Satin Charcoal finish.

We've seen builds from Desert Power Wagons in the past using Cummins engines from heavy-duty Ram trucks, but this particular beast uses the high-powered Hemi from a Ram 1500 TRX . In standard form, a TRX delivers 702 horsepower and 650 pound-feet from its supercharged 6.2-liter V8. That wasn't enough, so it's now been fitted with a National Speed Stage-3 upgrade that gives it 1,000 hp and 925 lb-ft. Key changes include a new camshaft, upgraded valve springs and pushrods, a larger supercharger, long-tube headers, a 108 mm throttle body, and an improved fuel system. The TRX's TorqueFlite 8HP95 eight-speed automatic transmission remains, and this wild Power Wagon also retains the TRX's driving modes, including Rock, Baja, Tow, Auto Sport, Snow, and even launch control.

The interior shares most of its components with a TRX. However, the tuner has given it a classic vibe with Rich Pinecone Distressed leather on the seats, door cards, dashboard, and center console. A JL Audio system has been added, along with a Rolls-Royce-esque starlight headliner. Not only is this insane Ram-based showpiece fully functional, it's currently for sale. The price? An eye-watering $599,950.

title: At $18,900, Is This Incredibly Low-Mileage 1986 Chrysler LeBaron Town & Country A Woody You Would Buy?
raw_summary: With just 3,800 miles on the clock, today's Nice Price or No Dice LeBaron Town & Country is a true time capsule of '80s glory. It even has a bench seat in the front! Now priced about 30% more than when it was new, we'll have to decide whether it's worth it to feel the MTV-era vibes. With the introduction of the Prius in the late 1990s, Toyota rewrote the meaning of a "hybrid auto." Before the Prius mated electric and internal combustion motors for power, a hybrid auto typically meant an American engine in a European car. The Sunbeam Tiger with its British-built body and Ford 289 was a hybrid. So too were the Iso Rivolta and the clutch of Bizzarrini, which sported Chevy small-block power.

With the introduction of the Prius in the late 1990s, Toyota rewrote the meaning of a "hybrid auto." Before the Prius mated electric and internal combustion motors for power, a hybrid auto typically meant an American engine in a European car. The Sunbeam Tiger with its British-built body and Ford 289 was a hybrid. So too were the Iso Rivolta and the clutch of Bizzarrini, which sported Chevy small-block power.

The 2013 Cadillac Escalade we looked at on Thursday is a hybrid in the modern sense, featuring a gearbox employing two electric motors to aid the V8 engine in both driving the SUV and keeping its high-voltage battery full of electrons. That was, and still is, a fiddly system with a number of known failure points. On top of that, our Escalade already had 140K under its belt, so those failures could be expected at any given time. Those factors led to warnings in the comments and eventually, a 65% 'No Dice' loss for the Caddy's $11,995 asking price.

In the 1933 novel "Lost Horizon" by James Hilton, a small group of Westerners survives a plane crash high in a remote, uncharted part of the Himalayas. There, they discover a lamasery—Shangri-La—which seemingly has magical properties that slow aging among its inhabitants. This comes at a high cost: the inhabitants are trapped there, because leaving means rapidly aging and dying. I know, bummer.

Today's 1986 Chrysler LeBaron Town & Country looks like it was just magically freed from some mystical Shangri-La, as it appears in as-new, almost entirely original condition and has less than 4,000 miles on the clock. How did this come to be? The seller has a succinct recap in the ad:

Back in 1986 a man bought his wife the finest station wagon Chrysler produced, this LeBaron Town & Country TURBO wagon. She only drove it 1500 miles before parking it in the garage when she became ill, and ultimately passed. The car ended up in climate controlled storage at a Chrysler dealer for 30 years. Then during Covid it was brought back to life with a new gas tank, driven a couple hundred miles and ended up on consignment at World Wide Autos in Colorado.

The current owner bought the car four years ago, brought it to Georgia, and replaced all the rubber bits, fluids, and the non-working factory stereo. Other than those updates, this K Car is claimed to be just as it left the factory.

This Town & Country has the goods, too. An unexpected decal on the hood announces the engine: a 2.2-liter Chrysler four with fuel injection and a Garrett T03 turbocharger. The motor was factory-rated at 146 horsepower and 168 pound-feet of torque, which might not seem like all that and a bag of chips today, but back in the mid-'80s it was pretty impressive.

raw_summary: The incredible news just keeps coming after Tuesday's huge victory for everyone not named Elon Musk . After a little more than three years blighting our roads, filling divorce court parking lots, and getting recalled for all of its parts falling off , the Tesla Cybertruck is dead. Never trust Elon Musk further than you can throw him , but early Friday morning, Tesla's CEO tweeted that the company will wind down production of the Cybertruck before finally killing it once and for all at some point next year. Posting at 12:30 a.m. Texas Freedom Time, a very normal time that every major CEO is awake and making important business announcements, Musk tweeted , "Tesla will be winding down production of the Cybertruck at Gigafactory Texas around the middle of next year to make room for increased Cybercab production." So there's no word twisting or reading between the lines required. Tesla's Texas Gigafactory will cease production of the Cybertruck next year, and that's the only place Tesla builds the Cybertruck.

So there's no word twisting or reading between the lines required. Tesla's Texas Gigafactory will cease production of the Cybertruck next year, and that's the only place Tesla builds the Cybertruck.

Yes, you read that right, folks. The Tesla Cybertruck is dead, and Woke 3 killed it. The Jalopnik staff, Barack Obama, and Karl Marx drove to Elon's house and made him do it. We have that power now. There's lightning in our veins, fire in our eyes, and soon to be a path of destruction in our wake. If we can kill the Tesla Cybertruck, what can't we do? Universal healthcare? Abolishing the electoral college? Free trans for everybody? Finally receiving a sincere apology from my mom? In 2027, we're making it happen.

It wasn't like it's that crazy for a large, generally established, electric-only automaker to add a pickup truck to its lineup. While a Moscow move may be coming, Tesla's a U.S. company that builds a lot of its vehicles including the Cybertruckkk in the U.S., so Tesla never had to worry about that pesky Chicken Tax. And us U.S. Americans sure love buying our pickup trucks. In fact, it should have been a hit. A U.S.-built pickup truck should have printed money for Tesla, but instead, it's dead after 3 horrible, painful, eye-assaulting years.

But it didn't. After the first blush of sales, interest in the truck fell faster than a stock price after a phony product reveal. The problem was, while looks are subjective, Tesla never bothered to make the Cybertruck good. I used hyperbole when I said all the Cybertruck's parts kept falling off. Technically that isn't true. But it's more true than it should be for a vehicle available for sale to the public, driven on public roads. Tesla's May recall over Cybertruck wheels falling off wasn't even the only recall Tesla had to issue over parts falling off the Cybertruck .

The Cybertruck also famously couldn't survive a car wash , got its butt kicked off-road by a Ford F-150 , had still more parts flying off on the road , oh yeah, snapped its frame in an off-road test . You know, good, old-fashioned American truck stuff. The fact that, by the time the Cybertruck launched, Musk had gone mask off as a full-fledged operative for the far-right , spending hundreds of millions of dollars to get Donald Trump elected in exchange for a role gutting regulators , didn't help either. It turns out people who buy electric aren't on Musk's chosen political side.

What's best, from a Republican perspective , is to crush EVs, see them driven before you, and hear the lamentations of the EVs' women. So they aren't what business consultants would call "the most reliable buyers of electric pickup trucks." Throw in prices being far higher after launch than we were originally told , and it shouldn't be surprising that sales were almost as terrible as talking to the owners .

title: McLaren's 2027 F1 front wing breaks cover in Brazil
raw_summary: McLaren’s new front wing, which will be the same concept it launches its 2027 Formula 1 car with, has been revealed at the Brazilian Grand Prix. As part of an end-of-season push by the Woking-based squad to deliver continuous improvements to its MCL40, the squad has brought its latest upgrades to Interlagos.
summary: McLaren’s new front wing, which will be the same concept it launches its 2027 Formula 1 car with, has been revealed at the Brazilian Grand Prix. As part of an end-of-season push by the Woking-based squad to deliver continuous improvements to its MCL40, the squad has brought its latest upgrades to Interlagos.
article_paragraphs: McLaren’s new front wing, which will be the same concept it launches its 2027 Formula 1 car with, has been revealed at the Brazilian Grand Prix.
As part of an end-of-season push by the Woking-based squad to deliver continuous improvements to its MCL40, the squad has brought its latest upgrades to Interlagos.
This includes tweaks to its floor, an updated rear wing, but also a front wing that will form the starting point for next season’s MCL41.
The front wing is a change of concept for the team as it features many revisions across the spectrum of wing elements.
The attachment point for the main plane and the endplate has been revised to now run across the lower edge – where it marries up with the refined outboard element.

The attachment between the nose and the main plane has been adjusted to sit on the second flap now rather than the mainplane, while the new wing also features an adjustment in the height of the flap elements.
Speaking ahead of the weekend, McLaren explained that the changes delivered were about both delivering more downforce and improving car balance.
Chief technical officer of aerodynamics Peter Prodromou also made clear that these changes were the launchpad for its 2027 project.

raw_title: World’s First Production Car To Cross 500 Kmph – BYD Yangwang U9 Xtreme
title: World's First Production Car To Cross 500 Kmph
raw_summary: You might remember BYD Yangwang U9 which debuted a couple of years ago as the vehicle that featured DiSus-X intelligent body control system that could perform rhythmic body movements (basically dance) and then it also stole the limelight by jumping in the air to avoid potholes, making the world gawk at it. Now, a more extreme version of this Megacar called, BYD Yangwang U9 Xtreme, has just made headlines as the world’s first production car to cross the 500 km/h speed barrier on open roads ever. Yangwang U9 Xtreme did it by clocking 503.17 km/h in Abu Dhabi, UAE, marking a historic milestone and has been awarded with a Guinness World Record.
summary: You might remember BYD Yangwang U9 which debuted a couple of years ago as the vehicle that featured DiSus-X intelligent body control system that could perform rhythmic body movements (basically dance) and then it also stole the limelight by jumping in the air to avoid potholes, making the world gawk at it.
article_paragraphs: You might remember BYD Yangwang U9 which debuted a couple of years ago as the vehicle that featured DiSus-X intelligent body control system that could perform rhythmic body movements (basically dance) and then it also stole the limelight by jumping in the air to avoid potholes, making the world gawk at it.

Now, a more extreme version of this Megacar called, BYD Yangwang U9 Xtreme, has just made headlines as the world’s first production car to cross the 500 km/h speed barrier on open roads ever. Yangwang U9 Xtreme did it by clocking 503.17 km/h in Abu Dhabi, UAE, marking a historic milestone and has been awarded with a Guinness World Record.

There are sportscars, supercars and hypercars in the world, but BYD Yangwang U9 Xtreme is a Megacar, generating more than 1 MW of power (1,341 bhp). In fact, Yangwang U9 Xtreme is a multi-Megacar because it is rated at a peak power of 2,977 bhp, based on BYD’s 1200V e4 (Yi Si Fang) platform.

There are four motors powering Yangwang U9 Xtreme delivering 2,977 bhp of peak power and they can touch and bonkers 30,000 RPM. Combined, they deliver 1,200 bhp per tonne (power : weight ratio) and the torque vectoring system negates conventional axles and this system can adjust parameters at 100 times per second.

U9 Xtreme is a more performant version of BYD Yangwang U9 and it gets a host of updates in terms of aerodynamics to prevent it from flying, basically. These include a large carbon fiber front splitter, a dual-channel hood, tall swan neck rear spoiler and a massive diffuser. Yangwang U9 Xtreme gets unique graphics too and production is limited to just 30 units worldwide.

Last year in September, Yangwang U9 Xtreme locked 496.22 km/h top speed at Germany and then it clocked a sub 7 minutes lap time at Nurburgring Nordschleife (6m 59.157s), becoming the first mass produced electric supercar to achieve it. The new record was achieved at Abu Dhabi, UAE and it outdid itself by 6.95 km/h breaking the 500 km/h barrier at 503.17 km/h top speed.

Powering BYD Yangwang U9 Xtreme is an 80 kWh battery pack featuring a 30C discharge rate, this allows the battery to send enough juice across the 1200V and 1000A architecture to power four motors rated at 2,977 bhp.

In the video, we can see the professional driver warming up the tyres and increasing grip and traction for around a minute. And then he maintained the throttle around mid position till the vehicle reached 380 km/h and then he gunned it with full pedal to the metal till Yangwang U9 Xtreme hit 503.17 km/h top speed.

title: Liebherr expands excavator range with new, 250-tonne electric model
raw_summary: It takes some seriously heavy equipment to make an ultra-class mining truck look little , but that’s exactly what German equipment giant Liebherr does best, and its newest, 250-tonne production excavator keeps that tradition alive – only this time, it’s electric. Liebherr began converting its diesel-powered mining excavators to electric in limited numbers back in 2024 , and electric power has proven to be effective – moving millions of tons of dirt while saving millions of dollars in fuel and maintenance costs . Now, the company is translating that testing experience into regular production practice with the launch of a new, all-electric machine. Meet the R 9300 G8-E.
summary: It takes some seriously heavy equipment to make an ultra-class mining truck look little , but that’s exactly what German equipment giant Liebherr does best, and its newest, 250-tonne production excavator keeps that tradition alive – only this time, it’s electric.
article_paragraphs: It takes some seriously heavy equipment to make an ultra-class mining truck look little , but that’s exactly what German equipment giant Liebherr does best, and its newest, 250-tonne production excavator keeps that tradition alive – only this time, it’s electric.

Liebherr began converting its diesel-powered mining excavators to electric in limited numbers back in 2024 , and electric power has proven to be effective – moving millions of tons of dirt while saving millions of dollars in fuel and maintenance costs . Now, the company is translating that testing experience into regular production practice with the launch of a new, all-electric machine. Meet the R 9300 G8-E.

Based on the proven R 9300 G8 platform, the new Liebherr R 9300 G8-E packs an 850 kW (~1,140 hp) electric drivetrain designed to IEC standards and supports 6-6.6 kV power supplies. The company says its electric setup offers customers the same hydraulic power and bucket capacity (1.8 tonnes/cubic meter, or ~1.5 short tons/cubic yard) as the diesel version.

All that electric power ships with advanced electronics and operator assistance systems designed to maximize both efficiency and safety while giving mine operators more data to work and plan with. Liebherr describes its take on ADAS thusly:

The R 9300 G8-E comes with Liebherr Power Efficiency – Hydraulic Control as standard, which adapts hydraulic power to suit the machine’s load profile, reducing overall engine load factor. Thanks to its Generation 8 electronic architecture, the R 9300 G8-E is compatible with a range of Liebherr’s IoMine technology products, including its range of excavator Assistance Systems, the semi-autonomous Bucket Filling Assistant, the Skyview vision system as well as the data visualisation tool, Data View. Customers also have the option of installing Liebherr’s autonomous cable reel solution onto the excavator to assist with cable management and support machine mobility on site.

Like its repowered cousins , the big electric excavator does seem to have on-board batteries, but is primarily driven and operated with grid power, reducing charging and re-charging concerns and enabling round-the-clock operations for as long as grid power holds .

Liebherr touts the benefits of new R 9300 G8-E’s quiet, emissions-free running throughout its official announcement, but doesn’t stop there. The company says its EV, which makes do with thousands of fewer moving parts in its drivetrain, can also reduce maintenance requirements and associated operating costs in certain applications and site conditions while improving workplace conditions for the people who work in and around the machine.
The electric drivetrain also reduces vibration inside the cab, improving operator comfort, limiting fatigue, and potentially contributing to a safer working environment.

raw_title: Marquez quickest as Qatar MotoGP weekend kicks off
title: Marquez quickest as Qatar MotoGP weekend kicks off
raw_summary: MotoGP championship leader Marc Marquez led the way in the opening practice session of the Qatar Grand Prix, heading Marco Bezzecchi by a tenth of a second. Marquez led virtually the entire session on the dusty Lusail track, and ended up on a 1m52.278s. He never fitted a spare rear tyre - but neither did virtually anyone else, with no incentive to use up any of the valuable rubber in the less-representative daytime session (compared to Friday afternoon practice, the sprint and the grand prix all taking place in the evening under the lights). Fabio Di Giannantonio was third behind Marquez and Bezzecchi, four tenths down on the leader. Pedro Acosta was fourth as the lead KTM, but his RC16 seemed to either fail or run out of fuel in the end as he had to pull over to the side of the track. Jorge Martin, who had withdrawn from the Sepang weekend last time out due to his wrist fracture from Phillip Island, had a livelier start here, logging 16 laps and placing fifth. With the Yamaha riders absent as the manufacturer elected to skip Qatar, a total of 18 riders took part. Honda's new stand-in Jake Dixon was last of them, after crashing on his very first flying lap. But Dixon was just 3.1s off the pace in the end, so will have zero trouble clearing MotoGP's 105-percent pace rule for race eligibility.
